title.zh: 卷二十八 志第四 五行一
title.raw: 卷二十八 志第四 五行一 Volume 28 Treatises 4: Five Elements 1

sentences.zh: 志第四 五行一

translations.literal: Treatise 4, Five Elements 1.
translations.idiomatic: Treatise on the Five Elements, Part One.

translations.literal: (Water)
translations.idiomatic: (Water)

sentences.zh: 史志五行，始自《漢書》，詳錄五行傳說及其佔應。

translations.literal: The historical treatise on the Five Elements begins with the Book of Han, recording in detail Five Elements lore and its prognostications and correspondences.
translations.idiomatic: Dynastic histories have treated the Five Elements as a formal subject since the Book of Han, which set the pattern of cataloguing wuxing lore together with omens and their supposed political correspondences.

sentences.zh: 後代作史者因之。

translations.literal: Later historians followed this.
translations.idiomatic: Later compilers followed suit.

sentences.zh: 粵稽《洪範》，首敘五行，以其爲天地萬物之所莫能外。

translations.literal: Examining the Hong Fan, it opens with the Five Elements, for nothing in Heaven and earth and the myriad things can stand outside them.
translations.idiomatic: Turn to the Hong Fan: it opens with the Five Elements because nothing under Heaven and earth, nothing among the myriad things, lies outside their scope.

sentences.zh: 而合諸人道，則有五事，稽諸天道，則有庶徵。

translations.literal: Correlating them with the way of mankind, there are the Five Affairs; examining them against the way of Heaven, there are the various signs.
translations.idiomatic: Correlated with the human way, they yield the Five Affairs; measured against the celestial way, they yield the various signs.

sentences.zh: 天人相感，以類而應者，固不得謂理之所無。

translations.literal: That Heaven and man resonate and respond according to kind cannot be denied as having no basis in principle.
translations.idiomatic: That Heaven and humanity affect one another, and that like kinds answer to like, is not something reason can simply dismiss.

sentences.zh: 而傳說則條分縷析，以某異爲某事之應，更旁引曲證，以伸其說。

translations.literal: Yet the traditions minutely sort and analyze, taking such-and-such an anomaly as the correspondence to such-and-such an event, further adducing roundabout proofs to extend their doctrine.
translations.idiomatic: The received lore, however, sorts every omen into fine categories, assigns each anomaly to a specific event, and piles on indirect proofs until the argument stretches wherever its authors wish.

sentences.zh: 故雖父子師弟，不能無所牴牾，則果有當於敘疇之意歟。

translations.literal: Thus even between father and son, teacher and pupil, there can be no freedom from contradiction — can this truly accord with the intent of arranging the categories?
translations.idiomatic: Even fathers and sons, masters and disciples, contradict one another; whether any of this still serves the Hong Fan's purpose of ordering the categories is doubtful.

sentences.zh: 夫苟知天人之應捷於影響，庶幾一言一動皆有所警惕。

translations.literal: If one truly knows that the resonance of Heaven and man is swifter than shadow and echo, then perhaps in every word and act one would hold some caution.
translations.idiomatic: If rulers truly believed that Heaven's response came faster than shadow or echo, they might weigh every word and deed with care.

sentences.zh: 以此垂戒，意非不善。

translations.literal: To set forth admonition in this way — the intent is not ill.
translations.idiomatic: Used as a warning, the doctrine is not without good intent.

sentences.zh: 然天道遠，人道邇，逐事而比之，必有驗有不驗。

translations.literal: Yet the way of Heaven is remote, the way of man near; matching event to event, some must prove true and some not.
translations.idiomatic: Yet Heaven's way is distant and man's way is near; force every event into a one-to-one correspondence, and some cases will fit while others will not.

sentences.zh: 至有不驗，則見以爲無徵而怠焉。

translations.literal: When there is no verification, one takes it as lacking sign and grows heedless.
translations.idiomatic: When a predicted correspondence fails, people decide the signs mean nothing and slacken their vigilance.

sentences.zh: 前賢之論此悉矣。

translations.literal: The discourse of worthies of old on this is exhaustive.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier sages debated this point thoroughly.

sentences.zh: 孔子作《春秋》，紀異而說不書。

translations.literal: Confucius composed the Spring and Autumn Annals, recording anomalies but not writing out interpretations.
translations.idiomatic: Confucius compiled the Spring and Autumn Annals: he noted anomalies but refused to spell out their meaning.

sentences.zh: 彼劉、董諸儒之學，頗近於術數禨祥，本無足述。

translations.literal: The learning of Liu, Dong, and other such scholars drew rather near to numerology and auspicious portents — not worth narrating in themselves.
translations.idiomatic: The systems of Liu Xiang, Dong Zhongshu, and their school leaned heavily on numerology and lucky omens; in themselves they hardly merit retelling.

sentences.zh: 班氏創立此志，不得不詳其學之本原。

translations.literal: When Ban established this treatise, he had no choice but to set forth the origins of that learning in detail.
translations.idiomatic: When Ban Gu first opened this treatise category, he had to trace those doctrines to their roots.

sentences.zh: 而歷代之史，往往取前人數見之說，備列簡端。

translations.literal: Yet dynastic histories often took sayings the predecessors had seen several times and merely listed them at the head of entries.
translations.idiomatic: Later official histories often recycled the same handful of older glosses and pasted them at the head of each entry.

sentences.zh: 揆之義法，未知所處。

translations.literal: Weighing this against the standards of historiography, one cannot tell where to place it.
translations.idiomatic: Measured against proper historiographical practice, it is hard to see what such material is doing in the annals at all.

sentences.zh: 故考次洪武以來，略依舊史五行之例，著其祥異，而事應暨舊說之前見者，並削而不載云。

translations.literal: Therefore, arraying events from Hongwu onward, I follow in outline the Five Elements precedent of older histories, recording only auspicious anomalies and strange events, while cutting out both the corresponding events and earlier formulations of the old theories.
translations.idiomatic: I have therefore arranged events from the Hongwu reign onward, kept the old Five Elements format in outline, and recorded only the omens themselves; correspondences, earlier theories, and repeated precedents are all omitted.

sentences.zh: 《洪範》曰：「水曰潤下」。

translations.literal: The Hong Fan says: "Water is called moistening and descending."
translations.idiomatic: The Hong Fan says: "Water is named moistening and descending."

sentences.zh: 水不潤下，則失其性矣。

translations.literal: When water does not moisten and descend, it has lost its nature.
translations.idiomatic: When water fails to moisten and sink, it has lost its proper nature.

sentences.zh: 前史多以恆寒、恆陰、雪霜、冰雹、雷震、魚孽、蝗蝻、豕禍、龍蛇之孽、馬異、人痾、疾疫、鼓妖、隕石、水潦、水變、黑眚黑祥皆屬之水，今從之。

translations.literal: Previous histories mostly classified constant cold, constant yin, snow and frost, hail, thunder, fish calamities, locusts, pig calamities, dragon and snake calamities, horse anomalies, human afflictions, plague, drum omens, falling stones, flooding, water transformations, black omens and black auspicious signs all under Water; the present account follows them.
translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories grouped constant cold, prolonged yin, snow and frost, hail, thunder, fish portents, locusts, pig calamities, dragon-and-snake portents, horse anomalies, human deformities, plague, drum omens, meteorites, floods, transformations of water, and black omens and black auspices under Water; this account follows that taxonomy.

sentences.zh: ▲恆寒

translations.literal: ▲ Constant cold.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Constant Cold

sentences.zh: 景泰四年冬十一月戊辰至明年孟春，山東、河南、浙江、直隸、淮、徐大雪數尺，淮東之海冰四十餘里，人畜凍死萬計。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 4, winter, eleventh month wuchen through the first month of spring of the following year: in Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, Zhili, Huai, and Xu, snow piled several feet deep; the Huai eastern sea froze for more than forty li; humans and livestock frozen to death numbered in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 4, winter/X/wuchen through the next year's early spring: Shandong, Henan, Zhejiang, Zhili, and the Huai–Xu region saw snow several feet deep; the sea off eastern Huai froze for more than forty li; tens of thousands of people and animals died of cold.

sentences.zh: 五年正月，江南諸府大雪連四旬，蘇、常凍餓死者無算。

translations.literal: Year 5, first month: the prefectures of Jiangnan had continuous snow for forty days; in Suzhou and Changzhou those who froze or starved to death were beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 5/I: Jiangnan prefectures snowed without break for forty days; in Suzhou and Changzhou the dead from cold and hunger were beyond number.

sentences.zh: 是春，羅山大寒，竹樹魚蚌皆死。

translations.literal: That spring, in Luoshan great cold; bamboo, trees, fish, and shellfish all died.
translations.idiomatic: That spring Luoshan suffered extreme cold; bamboo, trees, fish, and mollusks all perished.

sentences.zh: 衡州雨雪連綿，傷人甚多，牛畜凍死三萬六千蹄。

translations.literal: In Hengzhou rain and snow continued unbroken; many people were injured, and cattle and livestock frozen to death numbered thirty-six thousand hooves.
translations.idiomatic: At Hengzhou rain and snow fell in an unbroken spell; many people were hurt, and 36,000 head of cattle and livestock froze to death.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年四月壬戌，開原大雨雪，畜多凍死。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 13, fourth month renxu: in Kaiyuan great rain and snow; many livestock froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13/IV/renxu: Kaiyuan had heavy rain and snow; many animals froze to death.

sentences.zh: 十六年七八月，越巂雨雪交作，寒氣若冬。

translations.literal: Year 16, seventh and eighth months: in Yuexi rain and snow fell together; cold air was like winter.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 16/VII–VIII: Yuexi saw rain and snow together, with winter-like cold.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年十一月，鄖陽大雪，至十二月壬戌夜，雷電大作，明日復震，後五日雪止，平地三尺餘，人畜多凍死。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 6, eleventh month: in Yunyang great snow; on the night of twelfth month renxu, thunder and lightning were greatly active; the next day thunder again; five days later the snow stopped; level ground had more than three feet; many humans and livestock froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 6/XI: Yunyang had deep snow; on the night of XII/renxu thunder and lightning broke out violently, thundered again the next day, and only after five more days did the snow stop, leaving more than three feet on level ground; many people and animals froze to death.

sentences.zh: 正德元年四月，雲南武定隕霜殺麥，寒如冬。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, fourth month: in Wuding, Yunnan, frost fell and killed wheat; cold was like winter.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1/IV: Wuding in Yunnan was struck by falling frost that killed the wheat; the cold was like winter.

sentences.zh: 萬曆五年六月，蘇、鬆連雨，寒如冬，傷稼。

translations.literal: Wanli year 5, sixth month: in Su and Song continuous rain; cold was like winter; crops were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 5/VI: Suzhou and Songjiang had unbroken rain, winter-like cold, and damaged crops.

sentences.zh: 四十六年四月辛亥，陝西大雨雪，橐駝凍死二千蹄。

translations.literal: Year 46, fourth month xinhai: in Shaanxi great rain and snow; two thousand camels froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 46/IV/xinhai: Shaanxi had heavy rain and snow; two thousand camels froze to death.

sentences.zh: ▲恆陰

translations.literal: ▲ Constant yin.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Constant Yin

sentences.zh: 洪武十八年二月，久陰。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 18, second month: prolonged overcast.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 18/II: prolonged overcast skies.

sentences.zh: 正統五年七月戊午、己未及癸亥，曉刻陰沉，四方濃霧不辨人。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year 5, seventh month wuwu, jiwei, and guihai: at dawn the sky was overcast and sunken; thick fog on all sides — people could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 5/VII/wuwu, jiwei, and guihai: at dawn the sky hung dark; fog on every side was so thick that people could not be told apart.

sentences.zh: 八年，邳、海二州陰霧彌月，夏麥多損。

translations.literal: Year 8: in Pi and Hai two prefectures yin fog lasted a month; summer wheat was much damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 8: Pi and Hai prefectures lay under yin fog for a month; much of the summer wheat was ruined.

sentences.zh: 景泰六年正月癸酉，陰霧四塞，既而成霜附木，凡五日。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 6, first month guiyou: yin fog blocked on all sides; afterward frost formed adhering to trees; altogether five days.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 6/I/guiyou: yin fog sealed every quarter; frost then clung to the trees for five days in all.

sentences.zh: 八年正月甲子，陰晦大霧，咫尺不辨人物。

translations.literal: Year 8, first month jiazi: overcast and dim, great fog; within a few feet one could not distinguish people or things.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 8/I/jiazi: the sky was dim and great fog rolled in; within arm's reach neither person nor object could be made out.

sentences.zh: 成化四年三月，昏霧蔽天，不見星日者累晝夜。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 4, third month: dusk fog covered heaven; sun and stars were not seen for many day-and-nights.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 4/III: dusk fog veiled the sky; for many day-and-night cycles neither sun nor stars appeared.

sentences.zh: 九年三月甲午，四月丁卯，山東黑暗如夜。

translations.literal: Year 9, third month jiawu, fourth month dingmao: in Shandong darkness was like night.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 9/III/jiawu and IV/dingmao: Shandong turned dark as night.

sentences.zh: 二十年五月丙申，番禺天晦，良久乃復。

translations.literal: Year 20, fifth month bingshen: in Panyu the sky was dim; after a long while it recovered.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 20/V/bingshen: Panyu's sky darkened and only after a long while cleared.

sentences.zh: 二十三年十二月辛卯，大霧不辨人。

translations.literal: Year 23, twelfth month xinmao: great fog — people could not be distinguished.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 23/XII/xinmao: heavy fog in which people could not be distinguished.

sentences.zh: 弘治十五年十一月，景東晝晦者七日。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 15, eleventh month: in Jingdong daytime dimness lasted seven days.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 15/XI: Jingdong had daytime gloom for seven days.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月辛亥，甘肅昏霧障天，咫尺不辨人物。

translations.literal: Year 16, fourth month xinhai: in Gansu dusk fog blocked heaven; within a few feet one could not distinguish people or things.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 16/IV/xinhai: Gansu was choked by dusk fog; within a few feet neither person nor object could be told apart.

sentences.zh: 十八年秋，廣昌大雨霧凡兩月，民病且死者相繼。

translations.literal: Year 18, autumn: in Guangchang great rain and fog for two months altogether; the people fell ill and died in succession.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 18, autumn: Guangchang had rain and fog for two months running; sickness and death followed one upon another.

sentences.zh: 正德十年四月，鉅野陰霧六日，殺谷。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 10, fourth month: in Juye yin fog for six days; grain was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 10/IV: Juye suffered yin fog for six days and lost its grain.

sentences.zh: 十四年三月戊午，陰晦。

translations.literal: Year 14, third month wuwu: overcast and dim.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 14/III/wuwu: overcast, dim skies.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年正月丁卯，日午，昏霧四塞。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 1, first month dingmao, at noon: dusk fog blocked on all sides.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 1/I/dingmao, at noon: dusk fog closed in on every side.

sentences.zh: 三年，江北昏霧，其氣如藥。

translations.literal: Year 3: north of the Yangtze, dusk fog; its air was like medicine.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 3: north of the Yangtze, dusk fog whose air smelled like medicine.

sentences.zh: 天啓六年六月丙戌，霧重如雨。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 6, sixth month bingxu: fog heavy as rain.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 6/VI/bingxu: fog so dense it fell like rain.

sentences.zh: 閏六月己未，如之。

translations.literal: Intercalary sixth month jiwei: the same.
translations.idiomatic: Intercalary VI/jiwei: the same.

sentences.zh: ▲雨雪隕霜

translations.literal: ▲ Rain, snow, and falling frost.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Rain, Snow, and Falling Frost

sentences.zh: 洪武十四年五月丁未，建德雪。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 14, fifth month dingwei: in Jiande, snow.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 14/V/dingwei: Jiande had snow.

sentences.zh: 六月己卯，杭州晴日飛雪。

translations.literal: Sixth month jimao: in Hangzhou on a clear day snow flew.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 14/VI/jimao: Hangzhou saw snow fall on a clear day.

sentences.zh: 二十六年四月丙申，榆社隕霜損麥。

translations.literal: Year 26, fourth month bingshen: in Yushe frost fell and damaged wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 26/IV/bingshen: Yushe was hit by falling frost that damaged the wheat.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年，鳳陽八衛二三月雨雪不止，傷麥。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 4: in Fengyang eight guards had rain and snow without stop in the second and third months; wheat was injured.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 4: Fengyang's eight guards had unbroken rain and snow in the second and third months; the wheat suffered.

sentences.zh: 天順四年三月乙酉，大雪，越月乃止。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 4, third month yiyou: great snow; after a month it stopped.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 4/III/yiyou: heavy snow that did not cease for a month.

sentences.zh: 成化二年四月乙巳，宣府隕霜殺青苗。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 2, fourth month yisi: in Xuanfu frost fell and killed green shoots.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 2/IV/yisi: Xuanfu was struck by falling frost that killed the young shoots.

sentences.zh: 十九年三月辛酉，陝西隕霜。

translations.literal: Year 19, third month xinyou: in Shaanxi frost fell.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 19/III/xinyou: Shaanxi had falling frost.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年十月，南京雨雪連旬。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 6, tenth month: in Nanjing rain and snow for ten days running.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 6/X: Nanjing had rain and snow for ten consecutive days.

sentences.zh: 八年四月庚申，榆社、陵川、襄垣、長子、沁源隕霜殺麥豆桑。

translations.literal: Year 8, fourth month gengshen: in Yushe, Lingchuan, Xiangyuan, Changzi, and Qinyuan frost fell and killed wheat, beans, and mulberry.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8/IV/gengshen: Yushe, Lingchuan, Xiangyuan, Changzi, and Qinyuan were struck by falling frost that killed wheat, beans, and mulberry.

sentences.zh: 辛酉，慶陽諸府縣衛所三十五，隕霜殺麥豆禾苗。

translations.literal: Xinyou: in thirty-five prefectures, counties, guards, and posts of Qingyang, frost fell and killed wheat, beans, and seedling grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8/IV/xinyou: thirty-five Qingyang prefectures, counties, guards, and garrisons were struck by falling frost that killed wheat, beans, and young grain.

sentences.zh: 九年四月辛巳，榆次隕霜殺禾。

translations.literal: Year 9, fourth month xinsi: in Yuci frost fell and killed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 9/IV/xinsi: Yuci was struck by falling frost that killed the grain.

sentences.zh: 是月，武鄉亦隕霜。

translations.literal: That month, in Wuxiang also frost fell.
translations.idiomatic: That month Wuxiang likewise had falling frost.

sentences.zh: 十七年二月壬寅，鄖陽、均州雨雪雹，雪片大者六寸。

translations.literal: Year 17, second month renyin: in Yunyang and Junzhou rain, snow, and hail; the largest snowflakes were six inches.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 17/II/renyin: Yunyang and Junzhou had rain, snow, and hail; the largest flakes measured six inches.

sentences.zh: 六月癸亥，雨雪。

translations.literal: Sixth month guihai: rain and snow.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 17/VI/guihai: rain and snow together.

sentences.zh: 正德八年四月乙巳，文登、萊陽隕霜殺稼。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 8, fourth month yisi: in Wendeng and Laiyang frost fell and killed crops.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 8/IV/yisi: Wendeng and Laiyang were struck by falling frost that killed the crops.

sentences.zh: 丙辰，殺谷。

translations.literal: Bingchen: grain was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 8/IV/bingchen: grain was killed.

sentences.zh: 十三年三月壬戌，遼東隕霜，禾苗皆死。

translations.literal: Year 13, third month renxu: in Liaodong frost fell; seedling grain all died.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 13/III/renxu: Liaodong was struck by falling frost; the seedlings all perished.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年三月甲子，郯城隕霜殺麥。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 2, third month jiazi: in Tancheng frost fell and killed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2/III/jiazi: Tancheng was struck by falling frost that killed the wheat.

sentences.zh: 辛未，殺禾。

translations.literal: Xinwei: grain was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2/III/xinwei: grain was killed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年四月己亥，固原隕霜殺麥。

translations.literal: Year 22, fourth month jihai: in Guyuan frost fell and killed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 22/IV/jihai: Guyuan was struck by falling frost that killed the wheat.

sentences.zh: 隆慶六年三月丁亥，南宮隕霜殺麥。

translations.literal: Longqing year 6, third month dinghai: in Nangong frost fell and killed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 6/III/dinghai: Nangong was struck by falling frost that killed the wheat.

sentences.zh: 萬曆二十四年四月己亥，林縣雪。

translations.literal: Wanli year 24, fourth month jihai: in Lin County, snow.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 24/IV/jihai: Lin County had snow.

sentences.zh: 二十六年十一月辛亥，彰德隕霜，不殺草。

translations.literal: Year 26, eleventh month xinhai: in Zhangde frost fell; it did not kill grass.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 26/XI/xinhai: Zhangde had falling frost but the grass was not killed.

sentences.zh: 三十八年四月壬寅，貴州暴雪，形如土磚，民居片瓦無存者。

translations.literal: Year 38, fourth month renyin: in Guizhou violent snow; shaped like earthen bricks; among dwellings not a single tile remained.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 38/IV/renyin: Guizhou had a blizzard whose flakes were shaped like clay bricks; not one tile remained on the houses.

sentences.zh: 四十四年正月，雨紅黃黑三色雪，屋上多巨人跡。

translations.literal: Year 44, first month: rain of red, yellow, and black snow; on roofs many giant footprints.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 44/I: snow fell in red, yellow, and black; on the rooftops there were many giant footprints.

sentences.zh: 崇禎六年正月辛亥，大雪，深二丈餘。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 6, first month xinhai: great snow, more than two zhang deep.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 6/I/xinhai: heavy snow more than two zhang deep.

sentences.zh: 十一年五月戊寅，喜峯口雪三尺。

translations.literal: Year 11, fifth month wuyin: at Xifeng Pass snow three feet.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 11/V/wuyin: Xifeng Pass had three feet of snow.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月，會寧隕霜殺稼。

translations.literal: Year 13, fourth month: in Huining frost fell and killed crops.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 13/IV: Huining was struck by falling frost that killed the crops.

sentences.zh: 十六年四月，鄢陵隕霜殺麥。

translations.literal: Year 16, fourth month: in Yanling frost fell and killed wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 16/IV: Yanling was struck by falling frost that killed the wheat.

sentences.zh: ▲冰雹

translations.literal: ▲ Hail.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Hail

sentences.zh: 洪武二年六月庚寅，慶陽大雨雹，傷禾苗。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 2, sixth month gengyin: in Qingyang great rain and hail; seedling grain was injured.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 2/VI/gengyin: Qingyang had heavy rain and hail that damaged the seedlings.

sentences.zh: 三年五月丙辰，蔚州大雨雹，傷田苗。

translations.literal: Year 3, fifth month bingchen: in Yuzhou great rain and hail; field seedlings were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 3/V/bingchen: Yuzhou had heavy rain and hail that damaged the field crops.

sentences.zh: 五年五月癸丑夜，中都皇城萬歲山雨冰雹，大如彈丸。

translations.literal: Year 5, fifth month guichou night: at the Central Capital imperial city's Longevity Hill, rain and hail; large as pellet balls.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 5/V/guichou night: at Longevity Hill in the Central Capital imperial park, hail fell as large as pellet balls.

sentences.zh: 七年八月甲午，平涼，延安綏德、米脂雨雹。

translations.literal: Year 7, eighth month jiawu: in Pingliang, Yan'an, Suide, and Mizhi, rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 7/VIII/jiawu: Pingliang, Yan'an, Suide, and Mizhi had rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 九月甲子，鞏昌雨雹。

translations.literal: Ninth month jiazi: in Gongchang rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 7/IX/jiazi: Gongchang had rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 八年四月，臨洮、平涼、河州雹傷麥。

translations.literal: Year 8, fourth month: in Lintao, Pingliang, and Hezhou hail injured wheat.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 8/IV: Lintao, Pingliang, and Hezhou were hit by hail that damaged the wheat.

sentences.zh: 十四年七月己酉，臨洮大雨雹，傷稼。

translations.literal: Year 14, seventh month jiyou: in Lintao great rain and hail; crops were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 14/VII/jiyou: Lintao had heavy rain and hail that damaged the crops.

sentences.zh: 十八年二月，雨雹。

translations.literal: Year 18, second month: rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 18/II: rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 永樂七年秋，保定、浙東雨雹。

translations.literal: Yongle year 7, autumn: in Baoding and eastern Zhejiang, rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 7, autumn: Baoding and eastern Zhejiang had rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 十二年四月，河南一州八縣雨雹，殺麥。

translations.literal: Year 12, fourth month: in one prefecture and eight counties of Henan, rain and hail; wheat was killed.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 12/IV: one Henan prefecture and eight counties were struck by hail that killed the wheat.

sentences.zh: 正統三年，西、延、平、慶、臨、鞏六府及秦、河、岷、金四州，自夏逮秋，大雨雹。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year 3: in six prefectures Xi, Yan, Ping, Qing, Lin, and Gong, and four prefectures Qin, He, Min, and Jin, from summer through autumn, great rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 3: Xi, Yan, Ping, Qing, Lin, and Gong prefectures and Qin, He, Min, and Jin prefectures had heavy hail from summer through autumn.

sentences.zh: 四年五月壬戌，京師大雨雹。

translations.literal: Year 4, fifth month renxu: in the capital great rain and hail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 4/V/renxu: the capital had heavy rain and hail.

sentences.zh: 五年四月丁酉，平涼諸府大雨雹，傷人畜田禾。

translations.literal: Year 5, fourth month dingyou: in the prefectures of Pingliang great rain and hail; humans, livestock, fields, and grain were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 5/IV/dingyou: Pingliang prefectures had heavy rain and hail that injured people, livestock, fields, and grain.

sentences.zh: 六月壬申至丙子，山西行都司及蔚州連日雨雹，其深尺餘，傷稼。

translations.literal: Sixth month renshen through bingzi: in Shanxi Regional Military Commission and Yuzhou consecutive days of rain and hail; depth more than a foot; crops were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 5/VI/renshen–bingzi: the Shanxi regional command and Yuzhou had hail day after day, piling more than a foot deep and damaging the crops.

sentences.zh: 八月庚辰，保定大雨雹，深尺餘，傷稼。

translations.literal: Eighth month gengchen: in Baoding great rain and hail; depth more than a foot; crops were injured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 5/VIII/gengchen: Baoding had heavy rain and hail more than a foot deep, damaging the crops.

sentences.zh: 景泰五年六月庚寅，易州大方等社雨雹甚大，傷稼百二十五里，人馬多擊死。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 5, sixth month gengyin: in Yizhou Dafang and other communities great rain and hail; very large; crops injured for one hundred twenty-five li; many humans and horses were struck dead.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 5/VI/gengyin: Yizhou's Dafang and neighboring communities were struck by enormous hail over 125 li of cropland; many people and horses were beaten to death.

sentences.zh: 六年閏六月乙巳，束鹿雨雹如雞子，擊死鳥雀狐兔無算。

translations.literal: Sixth year, intercalary sixth month, on yisi, Shulu hail like hen's eggs; birds, foxes, and hares struck dead beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 6, intercalary sixth month, yisi: hailstones the size of hen's eggs fell on Shulu, killing countless birds, foxes, and hares.

sentences.zh: 天順元年六月己亥，雨雹大如雞卵，至地經時不化，奉天門東吻牌摧毀。

translations.literal: Tianshun first year, sixth month, on jihai, hail large as hen's eggs; reaching the ground, long unmelting; the eastern finial plaque of Fengtian Gate was destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 1, sixth month, jihai: hail as large as hen's eggs struck the ground and lay unmelted for a long while; the eastern finial plaque of Fengtian Gate was shattered.

sentences.zh: 八年五月丁巳，雨雹。

translations.literal: Eighth year, fifth month, on dingsi, hail.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 8, fifth month, dingsi: hail fell.

sentences.zh: 成化元年四月庚寅，雨雹大如卵，損禾稼。

translations.literal: Chenghua first year, fourth month, on gengyin, hail large as eggs; grain damaged.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 1, fourth month, gengyin: egg-sized hail ruined the grain.

sentences.zh: 五月辛酉，又大雨雹。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on xinyou, again great hail.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 1, fifth month, xinyou: heavy hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 五年閏二月癸未，瓊山雨雹大如鬥。

translations.literal: Fifth year, intercalary second month, on guiwei, Qiongshan hail large as a dou.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 5, intercalary second month, guiwei: hailstones as large as a dou fell on Qiongshan.

sentences.zh: 八年七月丙午，隴州雨雹大如鵝卵，或如雞子，中有如牛者五，長七八寸，厚三四寸，六日乃消。

translations.literal: Eighth year, seventh month, on bingwu, Longzhou hail large as goose eggs, some like hen's eggs; among them five like oxen, seven or eight inches long, three or four inches thick; after six days they melted.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 8, seventh month, bingwu: Longzhou was struck by hailstones as large as goose eggs and hen's eggs alike; five were ox-sized, seven or eight inches long and three or four thick, and did not melt away for six days.

sentences.zh: 九年五月丁巳，雨雹如拳。

translations.literal: Ninth year, fifth month, on dingsi, hail like fists.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 9, fifth month, dingsi: hail fell in fist-sized stones.

sentences.zh: 十三年春，湖廣大雨冰雹，牛死無算。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, spring, Huguang great rain and hail; cattle died beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13, spring: heavy rain and hail swept Huguang, and cattle died beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 十九年六月乙亥，潞州雨雹，大者如碗。

translations.literal: Nineteenth year, sixth month, on yihai, Luzhou hail; the large ones like bowls.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 19, sixth month, yihai: hail fell on Luzhou, the largest stones bowl-sized.

sentences.zh: 二十年二月丙子，清遠雨雹，大如拳。

translations.literal: Twentieth year, second month, on bingzi, Qingyuan hail large as fists.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 20, second month, bingzi: fist-sized hail struck Qingyuan.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，大雷電，復雨雹。

translations.literal: On bingxu, great thunder and lightning; hail again.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 20, bingxu: thunder and lightning broke overhead, and hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 二十一年三月己丑夜，番禺、南海風雷大作，飛雹交下，壞民居萬餘，死者千餘人。

translations.literal: Twenty-first year, third month, on jichou night, Panyu and Nanhai wind and thunder greatly arose; flying hail fell together; more than ten thousand dwellings ruined; more than a thousand dead.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 21, third month, jichou night: wind and thunder erupted over Panyu and Nanhai, hail raining down together; more than ten thousand homes were wrecked and more than a thousand people killed.

sentences.zh: 二十二年三月甲寅，南陽雨雹，大如鵝卵。

translations.literal: Twenty-second year, third month, on jiayin, Nanyang hail large as goose eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 22, third month, jiayin: goose-egg hail fell on Nanyang.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年三月壬申夜，融縣雨雹，壞城樓垣及軍民屋舍，死者四人。

translations.literal: Hongzhi first year, third month, on renshen night, Rongxian hail; city towers, walls, and military and civilian dwellings ruined; four dead.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 1, third month, renshen night: hail shattered city towers, walls, and both military and civilian houses in Rongxian; four were killed.

sentences.zh: 二年三月戊寅，賓州雨雹如雞子，擊殺牧豎三人，壞廬舍禾稼。

translations.literal: Second year, third month, on wuyin, Binzhou hail like hen's eggs; three shepherd boys struck dead; huts and grain ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 2, third month, wuyin: hen's-egg hail fell on Binzhou, killing three shepherd boys and wrecking huts and crops.

sentences.zh: 庚辰，貴州安莊衛大雷，雨雪雹，壞麥苗。

translations.literal: On gengchen, Guizhou Anzhuang Guard great thunder; rain, snow, and hail; wheat seedlings ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 2, gengchen: great thunder rolled over Anzhuang Guard in Guizhou; rain, snow, and hail followed, destroying the wheat.

sentences.zh: 四月辛卯，洮州衛雨冰雹，水涌三丈。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on xinmao, Taozhou Guard rain and hail; water surged three zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 2, fourth month, xinmao: rain and hail at Taozhou Guard sent floodwaters surging three zhang high.

sentences.zh: 四年三月癸卯，裕、汝二州雨雹，大者如牆杵，積厚二三尺，壞屋宇禾稼。

translations.literal: Fourth year, third month, on guimao, Yu and Ru prefectures hail; the large like wall-pounders; piled two or three chi thick; dwellings and grain ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 4, third month, guimao: hail in Yu and Ru prefectures—some stones as large as wall-pounders, heaped two or three chi deep—smashed houses and crops.

sentences.zh: 四月己酉，洮州衛雨雹及冰塊。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on jiyou, Taozhou Guard hail and ice blocks.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 4, fourth month, jiyou: hail and ice blocks fell on Taozhou Guard.

sentences.zh: 水高三四丈，漫城郭，漂房舍，田苗人畜多淹死。

translations.literal: Water three or four zhang high; inundating walls and towns; houses swept away; field seedlings, livestock, and people mostly drowned.
translations.idiomatic: The waters rose three or four zhang, drowning the walls and towns, sweeping away houses; crops, livestock, and people for the most part perished in the flood.

sentences.zh: 五年四月乙丑，莒、沂二州，安丘、郯城二縣，雨雹大如酒杯，傷人畜禾稼。

translations.literal: Fifth year, fourth month, on yichou, Ju and Yi prefectures, Anqiu and Tancheng counties, hail large as wine cups; people, livestock, and grain injured.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 5, fourth month, yichou: wine-cup hail struck Ju and Yi prefectures and Anqiu and Tancheng counties, injuring people, livestock, and grain.

sentences.zh: 六年八月己巳，長子雨雹，大者如拳，傷禾稼，人有擊死者。

translations.literal: Sixth year, eighth month, on jisi, Changzi hail; the large like fists; grain injured; people also struck dead.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 6, eighth month, jisi: fist-sized hail fell on Changzi, ruining the grain and killing people outright.

sentences.zh: 辛未，雨雹，大如彈丸，平地壅積。

translations.literal: On xinwei, hail large as pellets; heaped on level ground.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 6, xinwei: pellet-sized hail piled on the level ground.

sentences.zh: 八年二月壬申，永嘉暴風雨，雨雹，大如雞卵，小如彈丸，積地尺餘，白霧四起，毀屋殺黍，禽鳥多死。

translations.literal: Eighth year, second month, on renshen, Yongjia violent wind and rain, hail large as hen's eggs, small as pellets; piled on the ground more than a chi; white mist rose on all sides; dwellings ruined, grain killed; birds mostly dead.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, second month, renshen: a violent storm struck Yongjia, hail ranging from hen's eggs to pellets and heaping more than a chi deep; white mist rose on every side; houses were wrecked, grain destroyed, and birds died in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 三月己亥，桐城雨雹，深五尺，殺二麥。

translations.literal: Third month, on jihai, Tongcheng hail five chi deep; second wheat killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, third month, jihai: hail buried Tongcheng five chi deep and killed the second wheat crop.

sentences.zh: 己酉，淮、鳳州縣暴風雨雹，殺麥。

translations.literal: On jiyou, Huai and Feng prefectures and counties violent wind, rain, and hail; wheat killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, jiyou: wind, rain, and hail swept Huai and Feng prefectures and counties, destroying the wheat.

sentences.zh: 四月乙亥，常州、泗、邳雨雹，深五寸，殺麥及菜。

translations.literal: Fourth month, on yihai, Changzhou, Si, and Pi hail; five cun deep; wheat and vegetables killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, fourth month, yihai: hail five cun deep fell on Changzhou, Si, and Pi, ruining wheat and vegetables.

sentences.zh: 丙子，沂州雨雹，大者如盤，小者如碗，人畜多擊死。

translations.literal: On bingzi, Yizhou hail; the large like platters, the small like bowls; people and livestock mostly struck dead.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, bingzi: hailstones as large as platters and as small as bowls struck Yizhou, killing most of the people and livestock caught in the open.

sentences.zh: 六月乙卯，雨雹。

translations.literal: Sixth month, on yimao, hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, sixth month, yimao: hail fell.

sentences.zh: 七月乙酉，洮州衛雨冰雹，殺禾。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on yiyou, Taozhou Guard rain and hail; grain killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, seventh month, yiyou: rain and hail at Taozhou Guard destroyed the grain.

sentences.zh: 暴水至，人畜多溺死者。

translations.literal: Violent water arrived; people and livestock mostly drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Floodwaters rushed in; people and livestock for the most part drowned.

sentences.zh: 丙戌，甘肅西寧大雨雹，殺禾及畜。

translations.literal: On bingxu, Gansu Xining great hail; grain and livestock killed.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 8, bingxu: great hail struck Xining in Gansu, killing grain and livestock alike.

sentences.zh: 九年五月丙辰，雨雹。

translations.literal: Ninth year, fifth month, on bingchen, hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 9, fifth month, bingchen: hail fell.

sentences.zh: 十年二月己卯，江西新城雨冰雹，民有凍死者。

translations.literal: Tenth year, second month, on jimao, Jiangxi Xincheng rain and hail; among the people some froze to death.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 10, second month, jimao: rain and hail at Xincheng in Jiangxi left some of the people dead from cold.

sentences.zh: 三月丁卯，北通州雨冰，深一尺。

translations.literal: Third month, on dingmao, North Tongzhou rained ice a chi deep.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 10, third month, dingmao: ice a chi deep fell on North Tongzhou.

sentences.zh: 十三年八月戊子，雨雹。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, eighth month, on wuzi, hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 13, eighth month, wuzi: hail fell.

sentences.zh: 丙午，又雨雹。

translations.literal: On bingwu, again hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 13, bingwu: hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 九月壬戌，又雨雹。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on renxu, again hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 13, ninth month, renxu: hail fell again.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月丁酉，徐州、清河、桃源、宿遷雨冰雹，平地五寸，夏麥盡爛。

translations.literal: Fourteenth year, fourth month, on dingyou, Xuzhou, Qinghe, Taoyuan, and Suqian rain and hail; on level ground five cun; summer wheat all rotted.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 14, fourth month, dingyou: rain and hail left five cun on level ground at Xuzhou, Qinghe, Taoyuan, and Suqian, and the summer wheat rotted away entirely.

sentences.zh: 五月乙亥，登、萊二府雨雹殺禾。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on yihai, Deng and Lai prefectures hail killed grain.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 14, fifth month, yihai: hail destroyed the grain in Deng and Lai prefectures.

sentences.zh: 七月辛卯，雨雹。

translations.literal: Seventh month, on xinmao, hail.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 14, seventh month, xinmao: hail fell.

sentences.zh: 正德元年六月戊辰，宣府馬營堡大雨雹，深二尺，禾稼盡傷。

translations.literal: Zhengde first year, sixth month, on wuchen, Xuanfu Maying Fort great hail; two chi deep; grain all injured.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, sixth month, wuchen: hail two chi deep fell on Maying Fort in Xuanfu, ruining the grain entirely.

sentences.zh: 三年四月辛未，涇州雨雹，大如雞卵，壞廬舍菽麥。

translations.literal: Third year, fourth month, on xinwei, Jingzhou hail large as hen's eggs; huts, beans, and wheat ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 3, fourth month, xinwei: hen's-egg hail wrecked huts, beans, and wheat in Jingzhou.

sentences.zh: 四年五月甲午，費縣大雨雹，深一尺，壞麥谷。

translations.literal: Fourth year, fifth month, on jiawu, Fei County great hail; a chi deep; wheat and grain ruined.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 4, fifth month, jiawu: hail a chi deep fell on Fei County, destroying wheat and grain.

sentences.zh: 八年十月戊戌，平陽、太原、沁、汾諸屬邑，大雨雹，平地水深丈餘，沖毀人畜廬舍。

translations.literal: Eighth year, tenth month, on wuxu, Pingyang, Taiyuan, Qin, Fen and subordinate districts, great hail; on level ground water a zhang deep; people, livestock, and dwellings washed away and destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 8, tenth month, wuxu: great hail across Pingyang, Taiyuan, Qin, Fen, and their districts left a zhang of water on level ground, washing away and destroying people, livestock, and dwellings.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月甲戌，宣府大雨雹，禾稼盡死。

translations.literal: Eleventh year, sixth month, on jiaxu, Xuanfu great hail; grain all dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 11, sixth month, jiaxu: great hail in Xuanfu killed the grain outright.

sentences.zh: 九月丙申，貴州大雨雹。

translations.literal: Ninth month, on bingshen, Guizhou great hail.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 11, ninth month, bingshen: great hail fell on Guizhou.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月己亥，安肅大雨雹，平地水深三尺，傷禾，民有擊死者。

translations.literal: Twelfth year, fifth month, on jihai, Ansuzhou great hail; on level ground water three chi deep; grain injured; among the people some struck dead.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 12, fifth month, jihai: great hail at Ansuzhou left three chi of water on level ground, injured the grain, and killed some of the people outright.

sentences.zh: 十三年四月壬午，衡州疾風迅雷，雨雹，大如鵝子，棱利如刀，碎屋，斷樹木如剪。

translations.literal: Thirteenth year, fourth month, on renwu, Hengzhou violent wind and swift thunder, hail large as goose eggs, sharp-edged like knives; houses shattered; trees cut as if clipped.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 13, fourth month, renwu: violent wind and swift thunder drove goose-egg hail with knife-sharp edges through Hengzhou, shattering houses and shearing trees as if with scissors.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年四月甲申，雲南左衛各屬雨雹，大如雞子，禾苗房屋被傷者無算。

translations.literal: Jiajing first year, fourth month, on jiashen, Yunnan Left Guard and subordinates hail; large as hen's eggs; grain and houses injured beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 1, fourth month, jiashen: hen's-egg hail struck Yunnan Left Guard and its subordinate posts, injuring grain and houses beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 五月己未，蓬溪雨雹，大如鵝子，傷亦如之。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on jiwei, Pengxi hail large as goose eggs; injuries likewise.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 1, fifth month, jiwei: goose-egg hail fell on Pengxi with like devastation.

sentences.zh: 二年五月丁丑，大同前衛雨雹。

translations.literal: Second year, fifth month, on dingchou, Datong Front Guard hail.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2, fifth month, dingchou: hail fell on Datong Front Guard.

sentences.zh: 四年四月丁未，大同衛雨雹。

translations.literal: Fourth year, fourth month, on dingwei, Datong Guard hail.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 4, fourth month, dingwei: hail fell on Datong Guard.

sentences.zh: 五月戊子，固安雨雹。

translations.literal: Fifth month, on wuzi, Gu'an hail.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 4, fifth month, wuzi: hail fell on Gu'an.

sentences.zh: 五年五月甲辰，滿城雨雹。

translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: locusts at Changzhou, Zhenjiang, Huai'an, Yangzhou, and Henan.

translations.idiomatic: Year 46: the four southern metropolitan prefectures again suffered locusts.

translations.idiomatic: Year 47, eighth month: locusts at Jinan, Dongchang, and Dengzhou.

translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 1, seventh month: locusts at Shuntian.

translations.literal: Year 5, sixth month, at Jinan flying locusts blotted out the sky and field crops were all destroyed.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, sixth month: at Jinan flying locusts blotted out the sky and field crops were all destroyed.

translations.idiomatic: Year 6, tenth month: drought and locusts at Kaifeng.

translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 8, seventh month: locusts in Henan.

translations.idiomatic: Year 10, sixth month: locusts in Shandong and Henan.

translations.idiomatic: Year 11, sixth month: great drought and locusts at both capitals, Shandong, and Henan.

sentences.zh: 成化五年六月，河決杏花營，有卵浮於河，大如人首，下銳上圓，質青白，蓋龍卵也。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 5, sixth month, when the Yellow River burst at Apricot Blossom Camp, eggs floated on the river as large as human heads, tapered below and round above, blue-white in substance—said to be dragon eggs.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 5, sixth month: when the Yellow River burst at Apricot Blossom Camp, eggs floated on the river as large as human heads, tapered below and round above, blue-white in substance—said to be dragon eggs.

sentences.zh: 弘治九年六月庚辰，宣府鎮南口墩驟雨火發，龍起刀鞘內。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 9, sixth month, day gengchen, at the southern pass beacon tower of Xuanfu Zhen sudden rain and fire broke out; a dragon rose from within a sword scabbard.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 9, sixth month, gengchen: at the southern pass beacon tower of Xuanfu Zhen sudden rain and fire broke out; a dragon rose from within a sword scabbard.

sentences.zh: 十八年五月辛卯，日午，旋風大起，雲翳三殿，若有人騎龍入雲者。

translations.literal: Year 18, fifth month, day xinmao, at noon a great whirlwind arose; clouds shrouded the three halls as if someone riding a dragon entered the clouds.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18, fifth month, xinmao, at noon: a great whirlwind arose; clouds shrouded the three halls as if someone riding a dragon entered the clouds.

sentences.zh: 正德七年六月丁卯夜，招遠有赤龍懸空，光如火，盤旋而上，天鼓隨鳴。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 7, sixth month, night of day dingmao, at Zhaoyuan a red dragon hung in the sky, light like fire, coiling upward; the celestial drum sounded with it.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 7, sixth month, night of dingmao: at Zhaoyuan a red dragon hung in the sky, light like fire, coiling upward; the celestial drum sounded with it.

sentences.zh: 十二年六月癸亥，山陽見黑龍，一龍吸水，聲聞數里，攝舟及舟女至空而墜。

translations.literal: Year 12, sixth month, day guihai, at Shanyang a black dragon was seen; one dragon sucked water with a sound heard for several li, lifting boats and boatwomen into the air then dropping them.
translations.idiomatic: Year 12, sixth month, guihai: at Shanyang a black dragon was seen; one dragon sucked water with a sound heard for several li, lifting boats and boatwomen into the air then dropping them.

sentences.zh: 十三年五月癸丑，常熟俞野村迅雷震電，有白龍一、黑龍二乘雲並下，口中吐火，目睛若炬，撤去民居三百餘家，吸二十餘舟於空中。

translations.literal: Year 13, fifth month, day guichou, at Yuye Village in Changshu thunder, sudden wind, and lightning; one white dragon and two black dragons rode the clouds down together, spewing fire from their mouths, eyes bright as torches; they swept away more than three hundred dwellings and sucked more than twenty boats into the air.
translations.idiomatic: Year 13, fifth month, guichou: at Yuye Village in Changshu thunder, sudden wind, and lightning; one white dragon and two black dragons rode the clouds down together, spewing fire from their mouths, eyes bright as torches; they swept away more than three hundred dwellings and sucked more than twenty boats into the air.

sentences.zh: 舟人墜地，多怖死者。

translations.literal: Boat people fell to earth; many died of terror.
translations.idiomatic: Boat people fell to earth; many died of terror.

sentences.zh: 是夜紅雨如注，五日乃息。

translations.literal: That night red rain poured like a torrent; it ceased after five days.
translations.idiomatic: That night red rain poured like a torrent; it ceased after five days.

sentences.zh: 十四年四月，鄱陽湖蛟龍鬥。

translations.literal: Year 14, fourth month, flood dragons fought on Poyang Lake.
translations.idiomatic: Year 14, fourth month: flood dragons fought on Poyang Lake.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十年五月癸酉，青浦佘山九蛟並起，涌水成河。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 40, fifth month, day guiyou, at She Mountain in Qingpu nine flood dragons rose together, surging water into a river.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 40, fifth month, guiyou: at She Mountain in Qingpu nine flood dragons rose together, surging water into a river.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十四年七月戊申，舒城大雷雨，起蛟百五十八，跡如斧劈，山崩田陷，民溺死無算。

translations.literal: Wanli year 14, seventh month, day wushen, at Shucheng great thunder and rain; one hundred fifty-eight flood dragons arose, their tracks like axe-cleavage; mountains collapsed and fields sank; people drowned beyond count.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 14, seventh month, wushen: at Shucheng great thunder and rain; 158 flood dragons arose, their tracks like axe-cleavage; mountains collapsed and fields sank; people drowned beyond count.

sentences.zh: 是歲，建昌民樵于山，逢巨蛇，一角，六足如雞距，不噬不驚，或言此肥遺也。

translations.literal: That year, a Jianchang woodcutter on the mountain met a huge serpent with one horn and six legs like cock spurs; it neither bit nor fled; some said it was the Feiyi.
translations.idiomatic: That year, a Jianchang woodcutter on the mountain met a huge serpent with one horn and six legs like cock spurs; it neither bit nor fled; some said it was the Feiyi.

sentences.zh: 十八年七月，猗氏大水，二龍鬥於村，得遺卵，尋失。

translations.literal: Year 18, seventh month, at Yishi great flood; two dragons fought in a village; abandoned eggs were found, then lost.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18, seventh month: at Yishi great flood; two dragons fought in a village; abandoned eggs were found, then lost.

sentences.zh: 十九年六月己未，公安大水，有巨蛇如牛，首赤身黑，修二丈餘，所至堤潰。

translations.literal: Year 19, sixth month, day jiwei, at Gong'an great flood; a huge serpent like an ox, red head and black body, more than twenty zhang long; wherever it went dikes burst.
translations.idiomatic: Year 19, sixth month, jiwei: at Gong'an great flood; a huge serpent like an ox, red head and black body, more than twenty zhang long; wherever it went dikes burst.

translations.literal: Year 31, fifth month, day wuxu, at Licheng great rain; two dragons fought in the water; mountain rocks all flew; level ground water rose ten zhang.
translations.idiomatic: Year 31, fifth month, wuxu: at Licheng great rain; two dragons fought in the water; mountain rocks all flew; level ground water rose ten zhang.

translations.literal: Year 45, eighth month, at Qinghe Village in Anqiu blue-white dragons fought.
translations.idiomatic: Year 45, eighth month: at Qinghe Village in Anqiu blue-white dragons fought.

translations.idiomatic: ▲ Horse anomalies.

translations.literal: Yongle year 18, ninth month, Zhucheng presented a dragon horse.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 18, ninth month: Zhucheng presented a dragon horse.

sentences.zh: 民有牝馬牧于海濱，一日雲霧晦冥，有物蜿蜒與馬接。

translations.idiomatic: A commoner had a mare pastured on the seashore; one day clouds and mist darkened; something sinuous coupled with the mare.

sentences.zh: 產駒，具龍文，其色青蒼，謂之龍馬云。

translations.literal: It foaled a colt bearing dragon markings, blue-green in color, called a dragon horse.
translations.idiomatic: It foaled a colt bearing dragon markings, blue-green in color, called a dragon horse.

translations.idiomatic: Xuande 7, fifth month: at Xinzhou commoner Wu Huan's household a mare foaled a colt with deer ears, ox tail, jade face, and jade hooves, flesh marked over the body like scales.

translations.literal: Seventh month, at Cangzhou an official stud mare foaled twin colts; the prefecture took it as auspicious and presented it to court.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: at Cangzhou an official stud mare foaled twin colts; the prefecture took it as auspicious and presented it to court.

sentences.zh: 宣宗曰：「物理之常，何足異也。」

translations.literal: The Xuan Emperor said: "It is the constant order of things—what is there to marvel at?"
translations.idiomatic: The Xuan Emperor said: "It is the constant order of things—what is there to marvel at?"

sentences.zh: 成化十七年六月，興濟馬生二駒。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 17, sixth month, at Xingji a mare foaled twin colts.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 17, sixth month: at Xingji a mare foaled twin colts.

sentences.zh: 弘治元年二月，景寧屏風山有異物成羣，大如羊，狀如白馬，數以萬計。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 1, second month, at Pingfeng Mountain in Jingning strange creatures gathered in herds, large as sheep, shaped like white horses, numbering in the tens of thousands.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 1, second month: at Pingfeng Mountain in Jingning strange creatures gathered in herds, large as sheep, shaped like white horses, numbering in the tens of thousands.

sentences.zh: 首尾相銜，迤邐騰空而去。

translations.literal: Head and tail linked, they wound away soaring into the sky.
translations.idiomatic: Head and tail linked, they wound away soaring into the sky.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖四十二年四月，海鹽有海馬萬數，岸行二十餘里。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 42, fourth month, at Haiyan tens of thousands of sea horses went ashore for more than twenty li.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 42, fourth month: at Haiyan tens of thousands of sea horses went ashore for more than twenty li.

sentences.zh: 其一最巨，高如樓。

translations.literal: The largest among them was as tall as a tower.
translations.idiomatic: The largest among them was as tall as a tower.

translations.idiomatic: Earlier histories often record cases of one birth yielding three sons; yet in recent years there have been many, too numerous to detail in full—only the somewhat unusual are recorded here.

translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 24, eighth month: at Longmen in Henan the woman Si Mudan had been dead three years; she revived by borrowing the corpse of Yuan Matou.

translations.literal: Xuande year 1, eleventh month, at the traveling palace Qi Rong's wife Pi of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard bore four sons in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: Xuande 1, eleventh month: at the traveling palace Qi Rong's wife Pi of the Embroidered-Uniform Guard bore four sons in one birth.

sentences.zh: 天順四年四月，揚州民婦一產五男。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 4, fourth month, a Yangzhou commoner's wife bore five sons in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 4, fourth month: a Yangzhou commoner's wife bore five sons in one birth.

sentences.zh: 成化十三年二月，南京鷹揚衛軍陳僧兒妻硃氏一產三男、一女。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 13, second month, Zhu of Nanjing Yingyang Guard soldier Chen Seng'er's wife bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13, second month: Zhu, wife of Nanjing Yingyang Guard soldier Chen Seng'er, bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月，宿州民張珍妻王氏臍下右側裂，生一子。

translations.literal: Year 17, sixth month, at Suzhou commoner Zhang Zhen's wife Wang; the right side below the navel split and a son was born.
translations.idiomatic: Year 17, sixth month: at Suzhou commoner Zhang Zhen's wife Wang; the right side below the navel split and a son was born.

sentences.zh: 二十年十二月，徐州婦人肋下生瘤，久之漸大，兒從瘤出。

translations.literal: Year 20, twelfth month, at Xuzhou a woman bore a tumor beneath the ribs; after long growth it enlarged; a child emerged from the tumor.
translations.idiomatic: Year 20, twelfth month: at Xuzhou a woman bore a tumor beneath the ribs; after long growth it enlarged; a child emerged from the tumor.

sentences.zh: 二十一年，嘉善民鄒亮妻初乳生三子，再乳生四子，三乳生六子。

translations.literal: Year 21, at Jiashan commoner Zou Liang's wife at first nursing bore three sons, at second nursing four sons, at third nursing six sons.
translations.idiomatic: Year 21: at Jiashan commoner Zou Liang's wife at first nursing bore three sons, at second nursing four sons, at third nursing six sons.

sentences.zh: 弘治十一年六月，騰驤左衛百戶黃盛妻宜氏一產三男一女。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 11, sixth month, Yi of Tengxiang Left Guard centurion Huang Sheng's wife bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 11, sixth month: Yi, wife of Tengxiang Left Guard centurion Huang Sheng, bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，應山民張本華妻崔氏生須長三寸。

translations.literal: Year 16, fifth month, at Yingshan commoner Zhang Benhua's wife Cui bore a beard three inches long.
translations.idiomatic: Year 16, fifth month: at Yingshan commoner Zhang Benhua's wife Cui bore a beard three inches long.

sentences.zh: 是時，鄭陽商婦生須三繚，約百餘莖。

translations.literal: At the same time, a Zhengyang merchant's wife bore a beard in three clusters, about a hundred-odd strands.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, a Zhengyang merchant's wife bore a beard in three clusters, about a hundred-odd strands.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二年六月，曲靖衛舍人胡晟妻生一男，兩頭四手三足。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 2, sixth month, at Qujing Guard houseman Hu Sheng's wife bore a male child with two heads, four hands, and three feet.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2, sixth month: at Qujing Guard houseman Hu Sheng's wife bore a male child with two heads, four hands, and three feet.

sentences.zh: 四年，橫涇農孔方協下產肉塊，剖視之，一兒宛然。

translations.literal: Year 4, at Hengjing farmer Kong Fangxie below the navel produced a lump of flesh; when cut open, a child was plainly visible within.
translations.idiomatic: Year 4: at Hengjing farmer Kong Fangxie below the navel produced a lump of flesh; when cut open, a child was plainly visible within.

sentences.zh: 五年，江南民婦生妖，六目四面，有角，手足各一節，獨爪，鬼聲。

translations.literal: Year 5, a Jiangnan commoner's wife bore a monster with six eyes and four faces, horns, limbs each of one joint, single claws, and a ghostly voice.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5: a Jiangnan commoner's wife bore a monster with six eyes and four faces, horns, limbs each of one joint, single claws, and a ghostly voice.

sentences.zh: 十一年，當塗民婦一產三男一女。

translations.literal: Year 11, a Dangtu commoner's wife bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: Year 11: a Dangtu commoner's wife bore three sons and one daughter in one birth.

sentences.zh: 十二年，貴州安衛軍李華妻生男，兩頭四手四足。

translations.literal: Year 12, at Guizhou Anwei Guard soldier Li Hua's wife bore a male child with two heads, four hands, and four feet.
translations.idiomatic: Year 12: at Guizhou Anwei Guard soldier Li Hua's wife bore a male child with two heads, four hands, and four feet.

sentences.zh: 二十七年七月，大同右衛參將馬繼舍人馬錄女，年十七化爲男子。

translations.literal: Year 27, seventh month, Ma Lu's daughter of Datong Right Guard deputy commander Ma Ji, age seventeen, transformed into a man.
translations.idiomatic: Year 27, seventh month: Ma Lu's daughter of Datong Right Guard deputy commander Ma Ji, age seventeen, transformed into a man.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年十二月，靜樂男子李良雨化爲婦人。

translations.literal: Longqing year 2, twelfth month, at Jingle the man Li Liangyu transformed into a woman.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 2, twelfth month: at Jingle the man Li Liangyu transformed into a woman.

sentences.zh: 五年二月，唐山民婦生兒從左脅出。

translations.literal: Year 5, second month, a Tangshan commoner's wife bore a child emerging from the left flank.
translations.idiomatic: Year 5, second month: a Tangshan commoner's wife bore a child emerging from the left flank.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年，淅川人化爲狼。

translations.literal: Wanli year 10, a man at Xichuan transformed into a wolf.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 10: a man at Xichuan transformed into a wolf.

sentences.zh: 十八年，南宿州民婦一產七子，膚髮紅白黑青各色。

translations.literal: Year 18, a Nansuzhou commoner's wife bore seven children in one birth, skin and hair in red, white, black, and blue-green hues.
translations.idiomatic: Year 18: a Nansuzhou commoner's wife bore seven children in one birth, skin and hair in red, white, black, and blue-green hues.

sentences.zh: 三十七年六月，繁峙民李宜妻牛氏一產二女，頭面相連，手足各分。

translations.literal: Year 37, sixth month, at Fanzhi commoner Li Yi's wife Niu bore twin daughters, heads and faces joined, hands and feet separate.
translations.idiomatic: Year 37, sixth month: at Fanzhi commoner Li Yi's wife Niu bore twin daughters, heads and faces joined, hands and feet separate.

sentences.zh: 四十六年，廣寧衛民婦產一猴，二角四齒。

translations.literal: Year 46, a Guangning Guard commoner's wife bore a monkey with two horns and four teeth.
translations.idiomatic: Year 46: a Guangning Guard commoner's wife bore a monkey with two horns and four teeth.

sentences.zh: 是時，大同民婦一產四男。

translations.literal: At the same time, a Datong commoner's wife bore four sons in one birth.
translations.idiomatic: At the same time, a Datong commoner's wife bore four sons in one birth.

sentences.zh: 崇禎八年夏，鎮江民婦產一子，頂載兩首，臀贅一首，與母俱斃。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 8, summer, a Zhenjiang commoner's wife bore a child with two heads on the crown and a head growing from the buttocks; mother and child both died.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 8, summer: a Zhenjiang commoner's wife bore a child with two heads on the crown and a head growing from the buttocks; mother and child both died.

sentences.zh: 十五年十一月，曹縣民婦產兒，兩頭，頂上有眼，手過膝。

translations.literal: Year 15, eleventh month, a Caoxian commoner's wife bore a child with two heads, eyes atop the head, and hands reaching the knees.
translations.idiomatic: Year 15, eleventh month: a Caoxian commoner's wife bore a child with two heads, eyes atop the head, and hands reaching the knees.

sentences.zh: ▲疾疫

translations.literal: ▲ Pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Pestilence.

sentences.zh: 永樂六年正月，江西建昌、撫州，福建建寧、邵武自去年至是月，疫死者七萬八千四百餘人。

translations.literal: Yongle year 6, first month, Jiangxi Jianchang and Fuzhou, Fujian Jianning and Shaowu from last year to this month, pestilence dead more than seventy-eight thousand four hundred persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 6, first month: from the previous year through this month pestilence at Jiangxi's Jianchang and Fuzhou and at Fujian's Jianning and Shaowu killed more than 78,400 people.

sentences.zh: 八年，登州寧海諸州縣自正月至六月，疫死者六千餘人。

translations.literal: Year 8, Dengzhou Ninghai and other prefectures and counties from first month to sixth month, pestilence dead more than six thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 8: from the first month to the sixth month pestilence in Ninghai and other districts of Dengzhou killed more than 6,000 people.

sentences.zh: 邵武比歲大疫，至是年冬，死絕者萬二千戶。

translations.literal: Shaowu several years great pestilence; by this year winter, households extinguished twelve thousand.
translations.idiomatic: Shaowu had suffered great pestilence for years; by winter of this year 12,000 households were wiped out.

sentences.zh: 九年七月，河南、陝西疫。

translations.literal: Year 9, seventh month, Henan and Shaanxi pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 9, seventh month: pestilence in Henan and Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 十一年六月，湖州三縣疫。

translations.literal: Year 11, sixth month, Huzhou three counties pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Yongle 11, sixth month: pestilence in three counties of Huzhou.

sentences.zh: 七月，寧波五縣疫。

translations.literal: Seventh month, Ningbo five counties pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Seventh month: pestilence in five counties of Ningbo.

sentences.zh: 正統九年冬，紹興、寧波、台州瘟疫大作，及明年，死者三萬餘人。

translations.literal: Zhengtong year 9, winter, Shaoxing, Ningbo, and Taizhou great pestilence; by the next year dead more than thirty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengtong 9, winter: great pestilence at Shaoxing, Ningbo, and Taizhou; by the following year more than 30,000 had died.

sentences.zh: 景泰四年冬，建昌、武昌、漢陽疫。

translations.literal: Jingtai year 4, winter, Jianchang, Wuchang, and Hanyang pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 4, winter: pestilence at Jianchang, Wuchang, and Hanyang.

sentences.zh: 六年四月，西安、平涼疫。

translations.literal: Year 6, fourth month, Xi'an and Pingliang pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 6, fourth month: pestilence at Xi'an and Pingliang.

sentences.zh: 七年五月，桂林疫死者二萬餘人。

translations.literal: Year 7, fifth month, Guilin pestilence dead more than twenty thousand persons.
translations.idiomatic: Jingtai 7, fifth month: pestilence at Guilin killed more than 20,000 people.

sentences.zh: 天順五年四月，陝西疫。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 5, fourth month, Shaanxi pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 5, fourth month: pestilence in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 成化十一年八月，福建大疫，延及江西，死者無算。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 11, eighth month, Fujian great pestilence, extending to Jiangxi; dead beyond counting.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 11, eighth month: great pestilence in Fujian spread into Jiangxi; the dead were beyond counting.

sentences.zh: 正德元年六月，湖廣平溪、清涼、鎮遠、偏橋四衛大疫，死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, sixth month, Huguang Pingxi, Qingliang, Zhenyuan, and Pianqiao four guards great pestilence; dead very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, sixth month: great pestilence at the four guards of Pingxi, Qingliang, Zhenyuan, and Pianqiao in Huguang; casualties were very heavy.

sentences.zh: 靖州諸處自七月至十二月大疫，建寧、邵武自八月始亦大疫。

translations.literal: Jingzhou and other places from seventh month to twelfth month great pestilence; Jianning and Shaowu from eighth month also great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: From the seventh month to the twelfth, great pestilence raged in Jingzhou and neighboring districts; from the eighth month Jianning and Shaowu were likewise stricken.

sentences.zh: 十二年十月，泉州大疫。

translations.literal: Year 12, tenth month, Quanzhou great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 12, tenth month: great pestilence at Quanzhou.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖元年二月，陝西大疫。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 1, second month, Shaanxi great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 1, second month: great pestilence in Shaanxi.

sentences.zh: 二年七月，南京大疫，軍民死者甚衆。

translations.literal: Year 2, seventh month, Nanjing great pestilence; military and civilians dead very numerous.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 2, seventh month: great pestilence at Nanjing; soldiers and civilians died in great numbers.

sentences.zh: 四年九月，山東疫死者四千一百二十八人。

translations.literal: Year 4, ninth month, Shandong pestilence dead four thousand one hundred twenty-eight persons.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 4, ninth month: pestilence in Shandong killed 4,128 people.

sentences.zh: 三十三年四月，都城內外大疫。

translations.literal: Year 33, fourth month, inside and outside the capital great pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 33, fourth month: great pestilence within and beyond the capital.

sentences.zh: 四十四年正月，京師飢且疫。

translations.literal: Year 44, first month, capital famine and also pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 44, first month: famine and pestilence together in the capital.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十年四月，京師疫。

translations.literal: Wanli year 10, fourth month, capital pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 10, fourth month: pestilence in the capital.

sentences.zh: 十五年五月，又疫。

translations.literal: Year 15, fifth month, again pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 15, fifth month: pestilence struck again.

sentences.zh: 十六年五月，山東、陝西、山西、浙江俱大旱疫。

translations.literal: Year 16, fifth month, Shandong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Zhejiang all great drought and pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 16, fifth month: Shandong, Shaanxi, Shanxi, and Zhejiang all suffered great drought and pestilence.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十六年，京師大疫，自二月至九月止。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 16, capital great pestilence, from second month to ninth month stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 16: great pestilence in the capital raged from the second month until it abated in the ninth.

sentences.zh: 明年春，北畿、山東疫。

translations.literal: Next year spring, North Metropolitan Region and Shandong pestilence.
translations.idiomatic: The following spring: pestilence in the North Metropolitan Region and Shandong.

sentences.zh: ▲鼓妖

translations.literal: ▲ Drum omens.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Drum omens.

sentences.zh: 洪武五年八月己酉，徐溝西北空中有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 5, eighth month, on jiyou, Xu'gou northwest empty sky had sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 5, eighth month, jiyou: in the empty sky northwest of Xu'gou a sound like thunder was heard.

sentences.zh: 十一年，瑞昌有大聲如鍾，自天而下，無形。

translations.literal: Year 11, Ruichang had great sound like a bell, from the sky downward, formless.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 11: at Ruichang a great bell-like sound descended from the sky, though nothing was seen.

sentences.zh: 天順六年九月乙巳夜，天無雲，西北方有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Tianshun year 6, ninth month, on yisi night, sky without clouds; northwest had sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 6, ninth month, yisi night: though the sky was cloudless, the northwest resounded like thunder.

sentences.zh: 七年二月晦夜，空中有聲。

translations.literal: Year 7, last night of second month, sky had sound.
translations.idiomatic: Tianshun 7, last night of the second month: a sound in the sky.

sentences.zh: 大學士李賢奏，無形有聲謂之鼓妖，上不恤民則有此異。

translations.literal: Grand Secretary Li Xian memorialized: formless yet with sound is called drum omen; when the ruler does not pity the people, then this anomaly occurs.
translations.idiomatic: Grand Secretary Li Xian memorialized, "Sound without visible cause is called a drum omen; when the ruler fails to care for the people, this portent appears."

sentences.zh: 成化十三年正月甲子，代州無雲而雷。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 13, first month, on jiazi, Daizhou without clouds yet thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 13, first month, jiazi: thunder rolled at Daizhou though no clouds were present.

sentences.zh: 十四年八月戊戌，早朝，東班官若聞有甲兵聲者，辟易不成列，久之始定。

translations.literal: Year 14, eighth month, on wuxu, morning audience, eastern row officials as if heard armor and weapons sound; scattered not forming ranks; long after then settled.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 14, eighth month, wuxu: at morning audience the eastern row of officials seemed to hear the clash of arms; they broke ranks in alarm and only after a long while regained order.

sentences.zh: 弘治六年六月丁卯，石州吳城驛無雲而震者再。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 6, sixth month, on dingmao, Shizhou Wucheng post station without clouds yet quaked twice.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 6, sixth month, dingmao: though cloudless, Wucheng post station in Shizhou shook twice.

sentences.zh: 十七年六月甲申，江西廬山鳴如雷。

translations.literal: Year 17, sixth month, on jiashen, Jiangxi Lushan rumbled like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 17, sixth month, jiashen: Mount Lu in Jiangxi rumbled like thunder.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖二十九年二月甲子，隆慶州張山營堡山鳴。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 29, second month, on jiazi, Longqing prefecture Zhangshan camp fortress mountain rumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 29, second month, jiazi: the mountain at Zhangshan camp fortress in Longqing prefecture rumbled.

sentences.zh: 萬曆十二年十二月己未，蕭縣山鳴如驚濤澎湃，竟夜不止。

translations.literal: Wanli year 12, twelfth month, on jiwei, Xiao county mountain rumbled like surging billows, all night not stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 12, twelfth month, jiwei: a mountain in Xiao county boomed like surging billows and did not cease all night.

sentences.zh: 二十八年八月戊戌，西北方有聲如雷。

translations.literal: Year 28, eighth month, on wuxu, northwest had sound like thunder.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 28, eighth month, wuxu: the northwest resounded like thunder.

sentences.zh: 天啓七年八月丁巳，莊烈即位，朝時，空中有聲如天鼓，發於殿西。

translations.literal: Tianqi year 7, eighth month, on dingsi, Zhuanglie acceded; at court time, sky had sound like heavenly drum, issuing west of the hall.
translations.idiomatic: Tianqi 7, eighth month, dingsi: when Zhuanglie acceded, at court a sound like a heavenly drum rolled forth from west of the hall.

sentences.zh: 崇禎十二年十二月乙未，蕭縣山鳴。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 12, twelfth month, on yiwei, Xiao county mountain rumbled.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 12, twelfth month, yiwei: a mountain in Xiao county rumbled.

sentences.zh: 是月，西山大鳴如雷，如風濤。

translations.literal: That month, western hills great rumble like thunder, like wind and billows.
translations.idiomatic: That month the western hills thundered like a gale-driven sea.

sentences.zh: 十三年二月壬子，浙江省城門夜鳴。

translations.literal: Year 13, second month, on renzi, Zhejiang provincial city gate rumbled at night.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 13, second month, renzi: the gate of the Zhejiang provincial city rumbled at night.

sentences.zh: 十六年冬，建極殿鴟吻中有聲似鵓鳩，曰：「苦苦」，其聲漸大，復作犬吠聲，三日夜不止。

translations.literal: Year 16, winter, Jianji Hall owl-tail ornament within had sound like turtledove, saying "bitter bitter"; its sound gradually grew; again made dog-bark sound; three days and nights not stopping.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 16, winter: from the owl-tail ornament on Jianji Hall came a turtledove-like voice crying "bitter, bitter"; the sound swelled, then turned to barking, and for three days and nights did not cease.

sentences.zh: 明年三月辛丑，孝陵夜有哭聲，亦鼓妖也。

translations.literal: Next year third month, on xinchou, Xiaoling at night had crying sound; also a drum omen.
translations.idiomatic: The following year, third month, xinchou: crying was heard at night at Xiaoling—another drum omen.

sentences.zh: ▲隕石

translations.literal: ▲ Meteorites.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Meteorites.

sentences.zh: 成化六年六月壬申，陽信雷聲如嘯，隕石一，碎爲三，外黑內青。

translations.literal: Chenghua year 6, sixth month, on renshen, Yangxin thunder sound like whistling; meteorite one, broken into three; outside black inside green.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 6, sixth month, renshen: thunder at Yangxin whistled like a gale; one meteorite fell and split into three pieces, black outside and green within.

sentences.zh: 十四年六月辛亥，臨晉天鳴，隕石縣東南三十里，入地三尺，大如升，色黑。

translations.literal: Year 14, sixth month, on xinhai, Linjin sky rumbled; meteorite thirty li southeast of the county, entered earth three chi, large as a sheng measure, color black.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 14, sixth month, xinhai: the sky boomed over Linjin; a meteorite fell thirty li southeast of the county seat, buried itself three chi deep, was as large as a sheng measure, and was black.

sentences.zh: 二十三年五月壬寅，束鹿空中響如雷，青氣墜地。

translations.literal: Year 23, fifth month, on renyin, Shulu sky sound like thunder; blue qi fell to earth.
translations.idiomatic: Chenghua 23, fifth month, renyin: the sky over Shulu thundered; blue vapor struck the ground.

sentences.zh: 掘之得黑石二，一如碗，一如雞卵。

translations.literal: Digging obtained black stones two; one like a bowl, one like a chicken egg.
translations.idiomatic: When men dug, they found two black stones—one bowl-shaped, one egg-sized.

sentences.zh: 弘治三年三月，慶陽雨石無數，大小不一，大者如鵝卵，小者如芡實。

translations.literal: Hongzhi year 3, third month, Qingyang rained stones countless; sizes not uniform; large like goose eggs, small like foxnuts.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 3, third month: stones rained without number at Qingyang, ranging from goose-egg size down to foxnut size.

sentences.zh: 四年十月丁巳，光山有紅光如電，自西南往東北，聲如鼓，久之入地，化爲石，大如鬥。

translations.literal: Year 4, tenth month, on dingsi, Guangshan had red light like lightning, from southwest to northeast; sound like drum; long after entered earth, transformed into stone, large as a dou.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 4, tenth month, dingsi: at Guangshan a red flash like lightning streaked from southwest to northeast with a drum-like roar; long afterward it struck earth and turned to stone as large as a dou measure.

sentences.zh: 十年二月丙申，修武黑氣入地，化爲石，狀如羊首。

translations.literal: Year 10, second month, on bingchen, Xiuwu black qi entered earth, transformed into stone, shape like sheep head.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 10, second month, bingchen: black vapor plunged into the ground at Xiuwu and hardened into stone shaped like a ram's head.

sentences.zh: 十二年五月戊寅，朔州有聲，如迅雷，白氣騰上，隕大石三。

translations.literal: Year 12, fifth month, on wuyin, Shuozhou had sound like sudden thunder; white qi rose up; fell three large stones.
translations.idiomatic: Hongzhi 12, fifth month, wuyin: a thunderclap shook Shuozhou; white vapor shot upward and three large stones fell.

sentences.zh: 正德元年八月壬戌，夜有火光落即墨，化爲綠石，圓高尺餘。

translations.literal: Zhengde year 1, eighth month, on renxu, night had fire light fall at Jimo, transformed into green stone, round and one chi more in height.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 1, eighth month, renxu: at night a fiery light dropped on Jimo and became a green stone more than a chi high and round.

sentences.zh: 九年五月己卯，濱州有聲隕石。

translations.literal: Year 9, fifth month, on jimao, Binzhou had sound and meteorite.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 9, fifth month, jimao: a roaring fall at Binzhou left a meteorite.

sentences.zh: 十三年正月己未，鄰水隕石一。

translations.literal: Year 13, first month, on jiwei, Linshui meteorite one.
translations.idiomatic: Zhengde 13, first month, jiwei: one meteorite at Linshui.

sentences.zh: 嘉靖十二年五月丁未，祁縣有聲如鼓，火流墜地爲石。

translations.literal: Jiajing year 12, fifth month, on dingwei, Qi county had sound like drum; fire stream fell to earth and became stone.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 12, fifth month, dingwei: a drum-like sound at Qi county; a fiery streak struck earth and turned to stone.

sentences.zh: 四十二年三月癸卯，懷慶隕石。

translations.literal: Year 42, third month, on guimao, Huaiqing meteorite.
translations.idiomatic: Jiajing 42, third month, guimao: a meteorite at Huaiqing.

sentences.zh: 隆慶二年三月己未，保定新城隕黑石二。

translations.literal: Longqing year 2, third month, on jiwei, Baoding Xincheng fell black stones two.
translations.idiomatic: Longqing 2, third month, jiwei: two black stones fell at Xincheng in Baoding.

sentences.zh: 萬曆三年五月癸亥，有二流星晝隕景州城北，化爲黑石。

translations.literal: Wanli year 3, fifth month, on guihai, there were two shooting stars daytime falling north of Jingzhou city, transformed into black stone.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 3, fifth month, guihai: two shooting stars fell by day north of Jingzhou city and became black stone.

sentences.zh: 十七年九月戊午，萬載黑煙騰起，隕石演武廳畔。

translations.literal: Year 17, ninth month, on wuwu, Wanzai black smoke rose up; meteorite beside drill ground hall.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 17, ninth month, wuwu: black smoke billowed up at Wanzai and a meteorite fell beside the drill ground hall.

sentences.zh: 十九年四月辛酉，遵化隕石二。

translations.literal: Year 19, fourth month, on xinyou, Zunhua meteorites two.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 19, fourth month, xinyou: two meteorites at Zunhua.

sentences.zh: 四十四年正月丁丑，易州及紫荊關有光化石崩裂。

translations.literal: Year 44, first month, on dingchou, Yizhou and Zijing Pass had light transformed into stone, collapsed and cracked.
translations.idiomatic: Wanli 44, first month, dingchou: at Yizhou and Zijing Pass a flash of light turned to stone that split apart as it fell.

sentences.zh: 崇禎九年九月丁未，太康隕石。

translations.literal: Chongzhen year 9, ninth month, on dingwei, Taikang meteorite.
translations.idiomatic: Chongzhen 9, ninth month, dingwei: a meteorite at Taikang.

sentences.zh: ▲水潦

translations.literal: ▲ Floods.
translations.idiomatic: ▲ Floods.

sentences.zh: 洪武元年六月戊辰，江西永新州大風雨，蛟出，江水入城，高八尺，人多溺死。

translations.literal: Hongwu year 1, sixth month, on wuchen, Jiangxi Yongxin prefecture great wind and rain; flood dragon emerged; river water entered city eight chi high; many persons drowned.
translations.idiomatic: Hongwu 1, sixth month, wuchen: great wind and rain at Yongxin prefecture in Jiangxi; a flood dragon was seen; the river poured into the city eight chi deep and many drowned.

sentences.zh: 事聞，使賑之。
